agenda: Identical letters dated 19 January 2016 from the Permanent Representative of Colombia to the United Nations addressed to the Secretary-General and the President of the Security Council (S/2016/53); Report of the Secretary-General on the United Nations Verification Mission in Colombia (S/2025/595)
penholder: United Kingdom of Great Britain and Northern Ireland
members: United Kingdom of Great Britain and Northern Ireland

steps.by: United Kingdom of Great Britain and Northern Ireland
steps.intent: The United Kingdom’s objective is to secure a clean one-year extension of the Verification Mission’s existing mandate, with strong language on comprehensive implementation, WPS, child protection, human rights, rural reform, the Ethnic Chapter, and transitional justice. The main difficulty will be managing the wider deterioration in Colombia–United States relations without letting bilateral sanctions or counter-narcotics disputes contaminate a consensus text. We will also need to balance support for dialogue and possible ceasefire verification with respect for Colombia’s sovereignty and the principle of consent, while avoiding language that could invite a veto or erode the Council’s traditional unity on Colombia.

messages.Algeria: Algeria supports the extension of the Verification Mission's mandate until 31 October 2026 and welcomes the balanced draft. We ask the penholder to reinforce national ownership by making any ceasefire verification explicitly subject to the request of the Government of Colombia and agreement with the parties. We also suggest adding shared responsibility and international cooperation to the counter-narcotics paragraph, and reaffirming non-interference in the sovereignty paragraph.
messages.China: China supports the renewal of the Verification Mission's mandate and welcomes the UK's penholding. We ask that the text more clearly reflect the Government of Colombia's ownership and consent, consistent with the principle of respecting host-state sovereignty. We also suggest adding language on efficient and effective use of Mission resources, as China has consistently emphasized.
messages.Denmark: Denmark welcomes the UK draft and supports a one-year extension of the Verification Mission's mandate. We would like the text to include an explicit call for safe, unhindered and sustained humanitarian access and a survivor-centered reference to conflict-related sexual and gender-based violence. We also suggest adding women's organizations and age- and sex-disaggregated data to the reporting paragraph. With these modest additions, Denmark can support the draft.
messages.France: France supports the renewal of the Verification Mission's mandate and welcomes the balanced and comprehensive draft. We ask the penholder to include explicit language on sexual and gender-based violence in OP4, consistent with resolution 2754 and the Council's women, peace and security commitments. This is an important reinforcement, not a red line, and we are ready to support the text with that adjustment.
messages.Greece: Greece supports the extension of the Verification Mission and welcomes the balanced draft. We request stronger language on safe, timely and unimpeded humanitarian access and on survivors of conflict-related sexual and gender-based violence, consistent with international humanitarian law and the women, peace and security agenda. With those important additions, Greece can support the text.
messages.Guyana: Guyana supports the draft as a constructive basis for consensus and welcomes its focus on the Ethnic Chapter, rural reform and gender. We ask that OP2 explicitly include the full, equal and meaningful participation of Indigenous and Afro-Colombian peoples and their authorities, and that OP8 include reporting on the Government of Colombia's rapid response plan. These additions reflect Guyana's consistent emphasis on effective implementation and coordination and should not disrupt consensus.
messages.Pakistan: Pakistan supports the extension of the Verification Mission and welcomes the balanced text. We ask that OP1 make explicit the consent of the Government of Colombia and respect for Colombian national ownership, and that OP7 refer to coordination with the Government regarding Mission access. These changes reflect Pakistan's consistent emphasis on host-state consent and sovereignty while preserving the Mission's ability to implement its mandate.
messages.Panama: Panama supports the renewal of the Verification Mission and the balanced draft before us. Given our border with Colombia, we ask the penholder to strengthen language on safe humanitarian access and on regional cooperation to address displacement and cross-border humanitarian effects, with reporting on these issues. These additions would improve the Council’s response without altering the core mandate.
messages.Republic of Korea: The Republic of Korea supports the renewal of the Verification Mission’s mandate and welcomes the penholder’s balanced text. We would ask for two targeted additions: explicit language on ending the recruitment and use of children by armed groups in OP4, and safe and unhindered humanitarian access in OP7. We also suggest reflecting youth participation in OP8, consistent with the draft’s preamble. We can support the text with these adjustments.
messages.Russian Federation: The Russian Federation supports the extension of the Verification Mission’s mandate and considers the draft a balanced basis for consensus. We welcome the emphasis on full implementation of the Final Agreement and respect for Colombia’s sovereignty. We do not propose amendments at this stage and call on all Council members to avoid politicizing the Mission’s work.
messages.Sierra Leone: Sierra Leone supports the extension of the Verification Mission’s mandate and commends the United Kingdom for a balanced draft. We would like the text to reflect the Council’s partnership with the Peacebuilding Commission and to strengthen references to conflict-related sexual and gender-based violence and victims’ access to reparations. These additions would reinforce implementation of the Final Agreement and the Council’s broader conflict-prevention and peacebuilding commitments. We can support the draft with these adjustments.
messages.Slovenia: Slovenia welcomes the United Kingdom's draft and supports the 12-month extension of the Verification Mission's mandate. We ask for explicit language on safe and unimpeded humanitarian access and for strengthening the gender and child-protection reporting dimensions, including conflict-related sexual and gender-based violence. With these limited additions, Slovenia is ready to support the text.
messages.Somalia: Somalia supports the renewal of the Verification Mission’s mandate and the balanced text presented by the penholder. We welcome the emphasis on protection of civilians, children and women, rural reform, the Ethnic Chapter, and Colombia’s sovereignty and territorial integrity. We encourage the Council to maintain consensus and look forward to the Mission’s continued reporting.
messages.United States of America: The United States supports the renewal of the Verification Mission and remains committed to Colombia's peace process. However, we are deeply concerned by the surge in illicit drug production and trafficking and the continued attacks on security forces. We therefore request the changes above to strengthen counternarcotics language, explicitly condemn attacks by illegal armed groups, and ensure the protection of security personnel.

steps.summary: The revised draft accommodates the key cross-regional requests on humanitarian access, survivor protection, national ownership, counternarcotics and regional cooperation while preserving the Verification Mission’s mandate and Council unity. It is expected to command consensus and avoid any permanent-member veto.

Algeria.change: Replace with: Encourages the Government of Colombia to continue to address illicit drugs and related criminal economies through comprehensive and human rights-respecting approaches, including crop substitution and alternative development, with international cooperation and support, on the basis of shared responsibility and in full respect for the sovereignty and territorial integrity of Colombia;

messages.Algeria: Algeria supports the extension of the Verification Mission and welcomes the inclusion of language on ceasefire verification, non-interference, and shared responsibility in counternarcotics. To preserve the principle of Colombian ownership and avoid any punitive reading, we ask that OP8 be aligned with our earlier proposal: encourage rather than call upon Colombia to intensify efforts, and frame counternarcotics around human rights, alternative development, international cooperation, and shared responsibility. With that adjustment, Algeria can support the text.
messages.China: China supports the current text and thanks the penholder for incorporating language on Colombian ownership, consent, and efficient resource management. We believe the draft properly reaffirms the centrality of the Government of Colombia’s leadership and the Mission’s existing mandate, and we are ready to join consensus for its adoption.
messages.Denmark: Denmark supports the draft as revised and thanks the penholder for incorporating our proposals on humanitarian access, survivor-centred assistance and strengthened reporting, including on women's organizations and age- and sex-disaggregated data. The text provides a solid basis for renewing the Verification Mission's mandate for one year and for maintaining the Council's unified support for the 2016 Final Agreement. We encourage all members to support it.
messages.France: France supports the current draft and welcomes the penholder’s incorporation of our OP4 language on sexual and gender-based violence. We welcome the one-year extension of the Verification Mission and the text’s balanced focus on comprehensive implementation of the Final Agreement, rural reform, the Ethnic Chapter, transitional justice, protection of civilians and humanitarian access. France has no further changes and is ready to vote in favour.
messages.Greece: Greece thanks the penholder for incorporating humanitarian access in OP5 and for addressing survivor-centred protection through the dedicated provisions in OP7, which respond to our earlier concerns. The text as revised is balanced, reaffirms Colombian ownership, and strengthens protection and gender-responsive implementation; Greece can therefore support it as it stands and encourages the Council to adopt it by consensus.
messages.Guyana: Guyana supports the revised draft and thanks the penholder for incorporating our prior requests on Indigenous and Afro-Colombian participation and reporting on the rapid response plan. The text reflects the Council’s commitment to Colombian-owned implementation, the Ethnic Chapter, rural reform and humanitarian access. We see no further changes and are ready to join consensus.
messages.Pakistan: Pakistan supports the extension of the Verification Mission and the comprehensive implementation of the Final Agreement. We appreciate the penholder's partial acceptance of our earlier proposals, but we still consider explicit host-State consent essential for the Mission's mandate and deployment. We therefore request that OP1 expressly reflect the consent of the Government of Colombia, consistent with the principles of sovereignty, national ownership and non-interference; we can otherwise join consensus on the text.
messages.Panama: Panama supports the current draft and welcomes the incorporation of language on displacement, protection of displaced persons, regional cooperation and cross-border humanitarian reporting. We believe the text preserves Colombian ownership and the Mission’s mandate while addressing the humanitarian dimensions of the conflict, and we are ready to support its adoption.
messages.Republic of Korea: The Republic of Korea supports the current text and thanks the penholder for incorporating concerns on child recruitment and humanitarian access. We believe the draft appropriately renews the Verification Mission’s mandate and emphasizes full implementation, protection of civilians, and women’s and youth participation. We can join consensus and encourage continued close cooperation with the Government of Colombia.
messages.Russian Federation: The Russian Federation supports the adoption of the draft resolution as it stands. We value its reaffirmation of Colombian national ownership, sovereignty and non-interference, as well as its balanced treatment of counternarcotics on the basis of shared responsibility. We see no need for further changes and call on the Council to send a unified signal in support of the peace process in Colombia.
messages.Sierra Leone: Sierra Leone thanks the penholder for incorporating our earlier proposals on the Peacebuilding Commission, survivors of conflict-related sexual and gender-based violence, and reporting on reparations. We support the revised text as it stands, as it preserves Colombian national ownership, the consent of the Government of Colombia, and the comprehensive implementation of the Final Agreement. We encourage all Council members to join consensus on this mandate renewal.
messages.Slovenia: Slovenia supports the revised draft and welcomes the incorporation of our earlier humanitarian access and conflict-related sexual and gender-based violence reporting language. We believe the text provides a solid basis for extending the Verification Mission until 31 October 2026, with a strong focus on the Final Agreement, the Ethnic Chapter, rural reform, protection of civilians and women's full and equal participation. We are ready to join consensus.
messages.Somalia: Somalia supports the extension of the Verification Mission’s mandate and welcomes the balanced text, which reaffirms Colombian ownership, sovereignty and consent. We appreciate the emphasis on comprehensive implementation, protection of civilians, and regional cooperation respecting territorial integrity. Somalia sees no need for further amendments and is ready to support the draft as it stands.
messages.United States of America: The United States supports the current draft and thanks the United Kingdom for incorporating our priority concerns, including stronger language on counternarcotics, protection of security forces, and condemnation of the ELN and FARC dissidents. We believe the text appropriately extends the Verification Mission while respecting Colombian national ownership and consent. We look forward to voting in favour.

reasons.Algeria: Algeria supports renewing the UN Verification Mission and the peace process, consistent with its prior vote and sovereignty-focused positions. Its requested change to OP8 was partially accommodated, so voting in favour is consistent with its interests and Council record.
reasons.China: China has consistently supported the Colombia peace process and the Verification Mission’s mandate extensions, and the draft preserves Colombian ownership, government consent, and Council unity. There are no provisions requiring China to abstain or vote against.
reasons.Denmark: Denmark consistently supports UN peace verification mandates, Colombian peace implementation, gender and human rights provisions, and had already signalled support with no requested changes. A yes vote reflects its multilateral and human-rights-oriented foreign policy.
reasons.France: France consistently supports the UN Verification Mission and Colombia’s peace process, and the draft is balanced, respects Colombian consent and reflects France’s priorities on implementation, protection and gender. France therefore votes in favour.
reasons.Greece: Greece supports the extension of the UN Verification Mission and the Colombian-led peace process, consistent with its commitment to multilateral conflict resolution and protection of civilians. It had already indicated support for the draft and raised no objections.
reasons.Guyana: Guyana consistently supports the Colombian peace process and the Verification Mission, and the draft reflects its priorities on national ownership, the Ethnic Chapter, protection of civilians and respect for sovereignty. There is no reason for Guyana to oppose or abstain.
reasons.Pakistan: Pakistan supported the draft after its requested language on Colombian government consent was accepted. Voting yes aligns with Pakistan’s support for UN peace verification, national ownership, sovereignty and non-interference.
reasons.Panama: Panama has consistently supported Colombia’s peace process and the UN Verification Mission, and it requested no changes to the draft. It would vote yes to extend the mandate while emphasizing sovereignty, national ownership, and civilian protection.
reasons.Republic of Korea: ROK has consistently supported the Verification Mission and the draft aligns with its priorities on peace implementation, civilian protection, gender participation, and Colombian national ownership.
reasons.Russian Federation: Russia has consistently supported annual extensions of the UN Verification Mission in Colombia and the draft reflects its key concerns on sovereignty, national ownership, and consent. A supportive statement with criticism of unilateral sanctions aligns with Russian policy without blocking consensus.
reasons.Sierra Leone: Sierra Leone has consistently supported renewal of the Verification Mission and backed the draft in negotiations without requesting changes. A yes vote aligns with its post-conflict peacebuilding priorities and support for Colombian-led implementation.
reasons.Slovenia: Slovenia has consistently supported the Verification Mission and the Colombia peace process; it requested no changes and the draft reflects its priorities on human rights, gender, protection of civilians and national ownership. It would therefore vote in favour and likely explain its vote in a brief supportive statement.
reasons.Somalia: Somalia supports UN peace verification, protection of civilians and Colombian national ownership; the balanced draft aligns with its foreign-policy priorities, so it votes yes.
reasons.United Kingdom of Great Britain and Nort: The United Kingdom is the penholder and has consistently supported renewing the Verification Mission’s mandate by consensus, reflecting its priorities on the 2016 Final Agreement, gender, and civilian protection. Voting in favour is consistent with its established record and national interests.
reasons.United States of America: The United States has consistently supported the Colombia Verification Mission and the draft includes priority U.S. language on counternarcotics, sovereignty and regional security; a veto or abstention would be counterproductive despite bilateral tensions. Washington would likely vote yes while using its explanation of vote to press Bogotá on drugs and security.

before.Algeria: Algeria will vote in favour of this draft resolution. We support the renewal of the Verification Mission’s mandate and the comprehensive implementation of the Final Agreement, in full respect for Colombia’s sovereignty, national ownership and the principle of non-interference. We welcome the partial incorporation of our concerns in operative paragraph 8; at the same time, we emphasize that counter-narcotics efforts must be comprehensive, human-rights-respecting and based on shared responsibility, without undermining the sovereignty and territorial integrity of Colombia.
before.Denmark: Denmark votes in favour of this resolution. We welcome the continued extension of the United Nations Verification Mission in Colombia and reaffirm our support for the full implementation of the 2016 Final Agreement, including rural reform, the Ethnic Chapter, transitional justice, and comprehensive security guarantees. Denmark underscores the importance of the full, equal and meaningful participation of women, youth, Indigenous and Afro-Colombian peoples, and of ensuring protection of civilians, safe humanitarian access, and accountability for all violations. We thank the penholder for a balanced text that reaffirms Colombian national ownership and the consent of the Government of Colombia while supporting the Mission’s vital verification work.
before.France: France will vote in favour of the draft resolution renewing the mandate of the United Nations Verification Mission in Colombia. We thank the United Kingdom for its work and welcome the constructive engagement of the Government of Colombia. France remains fully committed to the 2016 Final Peace Agreement and to its comprehensive implementation, including rural reform, the Ethnic Chapter, transitional justice and the gender provisions. We are gravely concerned by continuing violence in conflict-affected areas, including in Catatumbo, and by attacks against civilians, social leaders, former combatants and members of the security forces, as well as by the recruitment and use of children. The Mission’s verification role and good offices remain essential. We call on all armed groups to cease hostilities, protect civilians and allow safe and unimpeded humanitarian access, and we stress the need to protect women, children, Indigenous and Afro-Colombian peoples. We reaffirm Colombia’s sovereignty and national ownership of the peace process, and we reiterate France’s support for dialogue in pursuit of peace.
before.Guyana: Thank you, Mr. President. Guyana thanks the United Kingdom for its work as penholder and for conducting inclusive consultations on this renewal. We support the extension of the mandate of the United Nations Verification Mission in Colombia, in close cooperation with and with the consent of the Government of Colombia and in full respect of Colombian national ownership. We welcome the draft’s emphasis on comprehensive implementation of the 2016 Final Agreement, including rural reform, the Ethnic Chapter, gender provisions, transitional justice, reincorporation and security guarantees for former combatants and communities. Guyana remains deeply concerned by continuing violence in conflict-affected areas, including in Catatumbo, and by its humanitarian impact, including displacement, confinement and the recruitment and use of children. We call on all armed actors to cease attacks against civilians, respect international humanitarian law and ensure safe and unimpeded humanitarian access. Guyana reaffirms the principles of sovereignty, non-interference and territorial integrity, and stresses that illicit drugs should be addressed through comprehensive, human rights-respecting approaches on the basis of shared responsibility. Guyana will vote in favour of the draft resolution.
before.Pakistan: Thank you, President. Pakistan will vote in favour of the draft resolution. We support the extension of the United Nations Verification Mission in Colombia, in full respect for Colombia’s sovereignty, national ownership and territorial integrity, and with the consent of the Government of Colombia. We welcome the progress made under the 2016 Final Peace Agreement and stress the importance of comprehensive implementation, including rural reform, the Ethnic Chapter, transitional justice, reincorporation, protection of civilians and assistance to victims. We also welcome the explicit reference to the consent of the Government of Colombia, which we believe is essential for the credibility and effectiveness of the Mission’s work. Pakistan remains committed to the peaceful settlement of disputes and to the central role of the United Nations in supporting nationally led peace processes.
before.Panama: Mr. President, Panama will vote in favour of this draft resolution. We reaffirm our support for the full implementation of the 2016 Final Peace Agreement, for Colombia’s sovereignty and national ownership, and for the Verification Mission’s work with the consent and close cooperation of the Government of Colombia. We also underscore the importance of protecting civilians, ensuring humanitarian access, and advancing regional cooperation in accordance with international law.
before.Republic of Korea: The Republic of Korea welcomes the Secretary-General’s report and the continued progress in implementing the 2016 Final Peace Agreement. We support the extension of the Verification Mission in close cooperation with and with the consent of the Government of Colombia, and we underscore the importance of protecting civilians, ensuring the safety of former combatants and communities, advancing rural reform and the Ethnic Chapter, and ensuring the full, equal and meaningful participation of women and youth. The Republic of Korea will vote in favour of the draft resolution.
before.Russian Federation: Mr. President, the Russian Federation supports the extension of the mandate of the United Nations Verification Mission in Colombia for another year. We take note of the Secretary-General’s report and welcome the continued implementation of the 2016 Final Agreement, while remaining concerned by ongoing violence and its humanitarian impact on civilians in conflict-affected areas. We stress that the Verification Mission must act strictly within its mandate, with the consent of and in close cooperation with the Government of Colombia, and in full respect for Colombia’s sovereignty and national ownership. We also reject unilateral coercive measures and external interference that complicate peacebuilding and international cooperation, including in the area of counter-narcotics. The Russian Federation will vote in favour of the draft resolution.
before.Sierra Leone: Mr. President, Sierra Leone votes in favour of this draft resolution. As a country that has known the ravages of conflict, we reaffirm our strong support for Colombia’s peace process, for the full implementation of the 2016 Final Agreement and for the vital work of the United Nations Verification Mission in Colombia. We welcome the extension of the Mission’s mandate and stress the importance of national ownership, sovereignty and territorial integrity, while calling on all armed groups to cease attacks against civilians, end the recruitment and use of children, and allow safe and unimpeded humanitarian access. We also underline the centrality of rural reform, the Ethnic Chapter, transitional justice, gender equality and the full participation of women, youth, Indigenous and Afro-Colombian peoples in building a stable and lasting peace.
before.Slovenia: Slovenia votes in favour of this draft resolution. We strongly support the renewal of the mandate of the United Nations Verification Mission in Colombia and the comprehensive implementation of the Final Agreement, including rural reform, the Ethnic Chapter, transitional justice, reincorporation and security guarantees. We welcome the resolution’s attention to the protection of civilians, children, survivors of conflict-related sexual and gender-based violence, human rights defenders and social leaders, as well as the full, equal and meaningful participation of women and youth. We underline the importance of safe and unimpeded humanitarian access, respect for Colombia’s sovereignty and national ownership, and human rights-based approaches to addressing illicit drugs. Slovenia remains committed to supporting Colombia’s peace process and the Mission’s work.
before.Somalia: Mr. President, Somalia supports the renewal of the mandate of the United Nations Verification Mission in Colombia. We welcome the progress reported under the 2016 Final Peace Agreement and underscore the need to protect civilians, including women, children, Indigenous and Afro-Colombian peoples, former combatants and social leaders, and to ensure safe and unimpeded humanitarian access. We stress that implementation must remain nationally owned, in close cooperation with and with the consent of the Government of Colombia, and in full respect for Colombia’s sovereignty and territorial integrity. Somalia therefore votes in favour of this draft resolution.
before.United States of America: The United States strongly supports the renewal of the mandate of the United Nations Verification Mission in Colombia and remains committed to the full implementation of the 2016 Final Peace Agreement. We welcome the draft resolution’s recognition of the urgent threat posed by illicit drug production and trafficking and its emphasis on regional security and Colombian ownership. At the same time, we remain deeply concerned by continued violence, including attacks against civilians, former combatants, human rights defenders and members of the security forces, and we call on all armed groups to cease such attacks immediately. We also urge the Government of Colombia to intensify comprehensive, human rights-respecting counternarcotics efforts and to cooperate closely with international partners. The United States will vote in favour of this resolution.

after.China:
Mr. President,

China welcomes the unanimous adoption of this resolution extending the mandate of the United Nations Verification Mission in Colombia until 31 October 2026. This reflects the Council’s firm support for the peace process in Colombia and the international community’s recognition of the Colombian Government’s efforts to advance peace through dialogue and national ownership.

China commends the Government of Colombia and the parties concerned for their continued efforts to implement the 2016 Final Peace Agreement. We support comprehensive implementation of the Agreement, including rural reform, the Ethnic Chapter, transitional justice, reincorporation and security guarantees for former combatants and communities. We believe that the Verification Mission should continue to carry out its mandate strictly in accordance with Council resolutions, with the consent of and in close cooperation with the Government of Colombia, and in full respect for Colombia’s sovereignty, independence, territorial integrity and national ownership.

China remains concerned by continuing violence in conflict-affected areas, including in Catatumbo, and by its humanitarian impact on civilians, including displacement and the recruitment and use of children. We call on all illegal armed groups to cease attacks against civilians, former combatants, social leaders and members of the security forces, and to ensure safe and unimpeded humanitarian access.

On counter-narcotics, China supports comprehensive and sustained efforts based on shared responsibility, alternative development and respect for the sovereignty and national circumstances of Colombia. The international community should provide constructive support to Colombia’s peacebuilding and development efforts, rather than resorting to unilateral coercive measures or external interference.

China also hopes that the Verification Mission will continue to strengthen its financial and human resources management, improve efficiency and effectiveness, and ensure the safety and security of its personnel. China stands ready to work with all Council members to support the peace process and long-term stability in Colombia.

Thank you, Mr. President.
after.Greece: Thank you, Mr. President. Greece voted in favour of this resolution and welcomes its adoption. We thank the United Kingdom for its work as penholder and the Secretary-General for his report. Greece remains firmly committed to the full implementation of the 2016 Final Peace Agreement, including comprehensive rural reform, the Ethnic Chapter, transitional justice, reincorporation and security guarantees for former combatants and communities. We underline that the Verification Mission must continue to act with the consent of and in close cooperation with the Government of Colombia, in full respect for Colombia’s sovereignty, territorial integrity and national ownership. Greece is gravely concerned by continuing violence in conflict-affected areas, including in Catatumbo, and by its humanitarian impact, especially on women, children, Indigenous and Afro-Colombian peoples. We call on all armed groups to cease attacks against civilians, former combatants, human rights defenders, social leaders and members of the security forces, to end the recruitment and use of children, and to ensure safe and unimpeded humanitarian access. We also stress the importance of the full, equal and meaningful participation of women and youth in the peace process and of comprehensive, human rights-based and shared-responsibility approaches to countering illicit drugs. Greece will continue to support Colombia’s peace, reconciliation and institution-building efforts.
after.United Kingdom of Great Britain and Nort:
Thank you, Mr President. The United Kingdom welcomes the unanimous adoption of this resolution and thanks Council members for their constructive engagement. As penholder, we are pleased that the Council has once again sent a clear and united signal of support for Colombia’s peace process and for the United Nations Verification Mission in Colombia. The extension of the Mission’s mandate until 31 October 2026, with the consent of and in close cooperation with the Government of Colombia, reaffirms Colombian national ownership and our shared commitment to the full implementation of the 2016 Final Agreement, including rural reform, the Ethnic Chapter, transitional justice, reincorporation, gender provisions and comprehensive security guarantees.

The United Kingdom remains gravely concerned by continuing violence in conflict-affected areas, including in Catatumbo, and by attacks against civilians, former combatants, human rights defenders and social leaders, as well as by the recruitment and use of children. We call on all armed groups, including the ELN and FARC dissidents, to cease attacks, respect international humanitarian law and allow safe and unimpeded humanitarian access. We also underscore the importance of accountability, protection of civilians, and the full, equal and meaningful participation of women, youth, Indigenous and Afro-Colombian peoples in building lasting peace.

The United Kingdom will continue to support Colombia and the Verification Mission in this vital work.
